This pattern localizes to the right lower limb and strongly implicates arterial insufficiency—not neuropathy, myopathy, or spinal stenosis. The Doppler ultrasound confirmation of *right femoropopliteal stenosis* provides direct anatomic and hemodynamic validation of flow-limiting atherosclerosis in the symptomatic limb. The patient’s age (55), male sex, and poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.2%, fasting glucose 142 mg/dL) are major, well-established risk factors for early, aggressive atherosclerotic PAD — particularly in the superficial femoral and popliteal arteries. The absence of red flags for mimics (e.g., no back pain, no bilateral/ascending symptoms, no sphincter dysfunction, no dermatomal sensory loss, no muscle atrophy or elevated CK) further reduces likelihood of neurogenic claudication, chronic inflammatory myopathy, or radiculopathy. No contradictory findings (e.g., normal pulses but severe stenosis on imaging, or discordant symptom laterality) undermine the coherence of the diagnosis.

[EVIDENCE]  
- Unilateral right calf cramps provoked by exertion and fully relieved by rest  
- Concomitant plantar tingling (a common ischemic paresthesia in PAD, distinct from neuropathic stocking-glove distribution)  
- Absence of neurological deficits: no numbness (beyond transient plantar tingling), no weakness, no foot drop, no gait instability  
- Doppler ultrasound confirms significant stenosis specifically in the right femoropopliteal arterial segment  
- HbA1c 7.2% and fasting glucose 142 mg/dL confirm suboptimal glycemic control, a key driver of accelerated atherosclerosis in PAD  
- Age 55 and male sex align with epidemiology of early-onset atherosclerotic PAD, especially with diabetes  

[GAPS]  
- Ankle-brachial index (ABI) value — not specified; would quantify severity (e.g., ABI 0.4–0.9 supports moderate-to-severe PAD) and serve as objective baseline  
- Resting vs. post-exercise duplex parameters (e.g., peak systolic velocity ratio, spectral broadening) — not detailed, though stenosis is confirmed  
- Presence/absence of palpable distal pulses (e.g., dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial) — not reported  
- Smoking history — stated as “if applicable” in counseling recommendation, but current status (current/former/never) is unspecified and highly relevant to risk stratification and progression  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Peripheral artery disease (PAD), right femoropopliteal stenosis, causing intermittent claudication.
